title: Stralsund
description: A Hanseatic port on the Baltic coast with a UNESCO-listed old town, a maritime economy and a university of applied sciences.
html:
A Hanseatic city on the Baltic

Stralsund sits on the Baltic coast opposite the island of Rügen, connected to it by a long bridge. Its brick Gothic old town is a UNESCO World Heritage site, and the harbour still shapes the economy: shipbuilding, maritime technology, fisheries and tourism are the main employers. The city has about 60,000 residents and a distinctly northern, unhurried character.

Studying and working here

The university of applied sciences is known for renewable energy, mechanical and electrical engineering, computer science and business, with a strong applied focus and some English-taught programmes. Living costs are among the lowest in Germany, and the beaches of Rügen are a short trip away. Berlin and Hamburg are both about three hours by train.
